name: maybe_Ui_TimeDisplayWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the play-time display window: resets the class table, releases the three animation references at +0x1380/+0x13D0/+0x1420, destroys the five 0x3B8-byte digit rows (six 0x9C panes each) and frees the object.
evidence: The old name claimed it owns a 'five-row list', but the rows are timer digits: 0x0075C1D4 (the table this function stores at self+0) also holds Ui_SetupTimeDisplay (0x0021E3E4) as a virtual method, and the 5 x 0x3B8 row / 6 x 0x9C pane layout matches Ui_TimerDisplay_Ctor (0x00411820). The embedded TimerDisplayPart table 0x00765420 (written by Ui_TimerDisplayPart_Ctor) is reset at the same time. Class is TimerDisplay-family, but this is not the already-named Ui_TimerDisplay (vtable 0x0076DD60), so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_RowList_Dtor
summary: Non-freeing destructor of the eleven-row list panel: clears the 11 x 0x148-byte row block, re-links the five intrusive list heads to empty and tears down the trailing embedded objects.
evidence: Only change to the previous wording is dropping the meaningless '_2' suffix. The now-named sibling 0x002298E4 (maybe_Ui_RowList_DeleteThunk, 20 bytes) is the deleting counterpart that frees this same object, so this is the plain D1 destructor; no named ctor exists, hence kept below 0.5.

name: Ui_MapWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the world-map window: releases the layout arena at +0x174, destroys the base object, releases the pack handle and the trailing sub-object, then frees the window.
evidence: Named Ui_MapWindow_Init (0x00240518) builds this same object 0x4BC earlier in the same class block, and the body's Pack_ReleaseHandle + layout release + free match a map window's stamp/layout ownership; nothing else in that block owns a layout arena at +0x174.

name: Ui_DialogRoot_DtorBase
summary: Base-object (D2) destructor of the dialog-root widget: reinstalls the class table 0x0075DC34, destroys the twelve 0x50-byte child widgets at +0x4C and runs the UI base destructor without freeing the block.
evidence: This is the exact inverse of the now-named Ui_DialogRoot_Ctor (0x00184E38): same class table 0x0075DC34, same twelve 0x50-byte children at +0x4C, same base. Its five callers are derived-class constructors/destructors (e.g. 0x001EB180) which build the dialog-root base subobject, which is what a D2 base-object destructor is for; the old name 'Ui_Widget_DtorB' was a placeholder.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DtorWithPanelArrays
summary: Deleting destructor of a composite window that owns two arrays of 0x414-byte Ui_Panel objects plus a message page: releases the layout references, destroys both arrays and the embedded objects, then frees the window.
evidence: The first pass read the class-table store and the array teardown as 'InitPartsL'; the body ends in Ui_Object_DtorBase + func_0010F6CC (free), so it is a destructor. It sits right after Ui_Window_CtorBase/Ui_Window_CtorBaseEx (0x002A4774/0x002A47AC), i.e. in the window base-class block, but no named ctor identifies the concrete class.

name: Ui_BattleCommandPopup_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the battle command popup: releases the cached text-table handle and the auxiliary buffer, destroys the child widget and frees the popup.
evidence: Named maybe_Ui_BattleCommandPopup_Create (0x004AA9A4) and the text-window helpers at 0x004AA704/0x004AACC0 bracket this block; the old '_DtorDelete' suffix is redundant, the body is a normal scalar deleting destructor (base dtor + free).

name: maybe_Field_DestroyNpcActionObject
summary: Deleting destructor of the large field NPC-action object: releases the child object at +0x324, destroys the embedded message page and a chain of embedded sub-objects, then frees the block.
evidence: No new named context identifies the concrete class: the containing vtable 0x007584E8 lists generic scene/widget virtuals (ToD, Ui_CampMenu_Setup, Ui_Layout_UpdateSubSlot) rather than a named action class, and the nearby thunk 0x001775C0 only runs the base destructor + free. The mechanism (message page + child object + free) is confirmed, the class name is not.

name: Ui_DialogRoot_DeletingDtorAlt
summary: Second deleting-destructor variant for the dialog-root layout: reinstalls table 0x0075DC34, destroys the twelve 0x50-byte children at +0x4C, runs the UI base destructor and frees the block.
evidence: It sits immediately after Ui_DialogRoot_Ctor (0x00184E38) and performs the same teardown as 0x00294820, but calls the base destructor at 0x001A6768 instead of 0x00291220, i.e. it is the variant emitted for a different base subobject of the same twelve-child layout. Named 'Field_ObjectDestructor' before, which said nothing about the class.

name: Ui_DialogRoot_DtorAlt
summary: Non-freeing complete-object destructor paired with 0x00184E84: reinstalls table 0x0075DC34, destroys the twelve 0x50-byte children at +0x4C and runs the base destructor, leaving the block to the caller.
evidence: Same class table and same twelve-child array as Ui_DialogRoot_Ctor (0x00184E38) and 0x00184E84, minus the final free, so it is the D1 complete-object variant. The old name 'Field_ObjectCleanup' guessed a field object without evidence.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWidget_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a composite UI widget: releases its three embedded layout/animation references, runs the base destructor and frees the object.
evidence: Only wording changed (verb phrase -> destructor name): the body is a plain widget teardown (three layout/anim releases, one child-object destructor, free). The neighbouring block (Sound_Listener_Dtor, Ui_BindGaugeParts, Ui_ActionWindow_Setup) gives no ctor for this class, so it stays maybe_.

name: Ui_Balloon_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the balloon widget: releases the two 0x348-byte record objects at +0x4C, runs the UI base destructor and frees the balloon.
evidence: It is slot 1 of vtable 0x007598D4 whose slot 0 is its non-freeing twin 0x001CA340 and whose other slots include the named Ui_Balloon_BindParts (0x001CA1C8); Ui_PanelCtor_vt1CA2EC (0x001CA238) constructs the same object. So the class is the balloon, not an anonymous 'Object'.

name: Ui_Balloon_Dtor

evidence: Slot 0 of vtable 0x007598D4, whose slot 1 (0x001CA304) frees the same object and whose named sibling Ui_Balloon_BindParts (0x001CA1C8) identifies the class.

name: maybe_Ui_MovieWindow_Dtor

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_DtorBody

Ui_ShopWindow_CreateSubObjects (0x001EAF6C) and Ui_ShopWindow_InitPanes build the same layout.

name: maybe_Ui_SingleLayoutObject_Dtor

name: maybe_Ui_CreditWindow_Dtor
